text:
Priya N.: Heads-up — ran a perf sweep on mixtral/qwen inference across a handful of customer chat templates and found repeated kernel flips mid-session. attaching quick profiler dump.
Marcus H.: ugh, kernel flips as in runtime switching kernels between tokens?
Priya N.: Yup. timeline shows switch from fast-attn kernel to fallback at ~token 42 for many requests, then back at ~token 89. p50 latency jumps ~1.7x during those windows.
Eve L.: Do we have a reproducible prompt? sounds like tokenizer-induced token count variance
Priya N.: Mostly long system messages + user history. Some templates include emoji + urls. tokenizer sometimes falls back to byte-run for segments -> token count + token type changes -> kernel estimator picks different kernel.
Li Chen: Also saw KV cache churn in the same traces — cache entries reallocated when kernel changed, which invalidates some prefetched KV layout and increases memcopy.
Marcus H.: Can you paste the profiler snippet?
Priya N.: ```
# profiler excerpt
request_id: r-09234
model: mixtral-8x
seq: 256->512 range
kernel_before: fast_attn_f32
kernel_after: attn_byte_fallback
p50: 18ms -> 31ms
kv_reallocs: 6
prefetch_hit_rate: 0.42
``` 
Eve L.: Interesting. Do we route by "estimated head dim" or by token length? Our kernel picker uses both heuristics and a tiny ML model that reads token_type bits.
Marcus H.: The tiny model gets confused when token_count jumps mid-request because it only sees the initial prefix distribution. if tokenizer later emits a byte-fallback span it triggers a re-eval and kernel switch.
Priya N.: Proposed mitigation: 1) compute a conservative kernel hint at compile time based on both prefix and potential byte-fallback probability, 2) sticky-kernel-per-request for first N tokens (like 128) to avoid mid-request flips, 3) group incoming requests by predicted post-tokenization length for batching.
Li Chen: Sticky kernel sounds low-risk. But we need a way to avoid pathological slowdowns if the chosen kernel is very bad for the rest of the sequence.
Eve L.: Maybe sticky + soft-recheck: keep sticky for N tokens, then re-evaluate at checkpoint tokens but only switch if projected improvement > 20% and memcopy cost < threshold.
Marcus H.: Also batching heuristics: dynamic batches currently group purely on arrival time/age. If we add a cheap hash of tokenized prefix length and tokenizer-mode (byte_fallback vs normal) into batch-keys we can reduce mixed-kernel batches.
Priya N.: I tried a quick experiment locally: bucketed by predicted tokens_mod_32 and token_mode, batch mix decreases from 28% to 6%, and latency tail improved.
Priya N.: sample config I used:
```
kernel_picker:
  sticky_tokens: 96
  recheck_interval: 64
  recheck_threshold_percent: 20
batching:
  bucket_keys: [predicted_len_mod_32, token_mode]
  max_delay_ms: 8
  max_batch_size: 64
```
Li Chen: Nice. Did you run this on dedicated infra or local GPU? would like to see effect on kv cache fragmentation
Priya N.: Local A100, dedicated reproducible run pending — infra-bot queued a canary with sticky-kernel + bucketed batching on stage.
infra-bot: Canary started: canary-1881234567-sticky-buckets on pool-stage-1. Expected run: 1h. Results will be in /canaries/1881234567.
Marcus H.: One more wrinkle: rope scaling differences between qwen / mixtral mean kernel numeric stability differs. If tokenizer adds extra BOS/EOS tokens (some chat templates wrap input differently) that changes positional indexing and may push into a RoPE-scaling-critical regime.
Eve L.: Right — special token placement + extra system prompt tokens altered the RoPE exponent applied and caused slightly different attention weight patterns. That can change which kernel is numerically safe.
Li Chen: Can we add a small tokenizer hook that marks when custom system wrappers are present and include that in kernel hint? e.g., `token_mode: chat_wrapped` vs `chat_plain`
Priya N.: I prototyped a tiny change in tokenizer service: return `token_mode` and `fallback_probability` in pre-tokenize stage. It's cheap and avoids a full tokenize per router.
Marcus H.: What's the risk? extra RPC on request path
Priya N.: It's local and cached; cost ~0.2ms per request.
Eve L.: Sounds worth it. Next steps?
Priya N.: 1) let canary run for 1h, check kv_reallocs, batch-mix rate, p95 latency. 2) infra: enable sticky kernel toggle and new batching buckets behind a flag. 3) devex: update prompt templates to avoid unnecessary leading/trailing special tokens where possible.
Li Chen: I'll watch kv metrics. If reallocs drop and memcopy bandwidth reduces we're good. I'll also add a metric for "kernel_switch_count" per request.
Marcus H.: I'll add the soft-recheck logic to kernel picker code and a test that simulates byte-fallback spans mid-sequence.
Eve L.: I'll prepare a short blurb for product about why some customer templates saw spikes and what we fixed.
Priya N.: Thanks all — will post canary link when infra-bot finishes. :thumbsup:
